headline: Southborough scheduled its upcoming town meetings, advanced school building and athletic projects, approved municipal pay rates, and finalized school labor contracts.
synopsis: The Select Board set the Fall Special Town Meeting for October 17, 2026, and the 2027 Annual Town Meeting for March 20, 2027, while approving $30,000 for a Route 9 wastewater study and rejecting a $105,000 police drone request. Regional school officials approved a $7.115 million bond sale for high school athletic facilities and announced a transition to school-issued Chromebooks paired with cell phone restrictions for fall 2026. The Elementary School Building Committee met with newly hired architects to plan tiered renovation options for the Neary School. Multiple boards also resolved personnel and compensation matters, including approving FY27 municipal pay rates, ratifying school support staff contracts, and granting Superintendent Greg Martineau a 3.5 percent raise.

highlights.title: Town Meeting dates set and wastewater study funded
highlights.why: The Select Board scheduled the Fall Special Town Meeting for October 17, 2026, and the 2027 Annual Town Meeting for March 20, 2027. The board also reallocated $30,000 from the Economic Development Committee budget for a Route 9 corridor wastewater financing study, while rejecting a $105,000 police drone system.

highlights.title: Bond approved for Algonquin athletic complex and cell phone ban planned
highlights.why: The Regional School Committee authorized a $7.115 million general obligation bond sale at a 3.07 percent interest rate to build the high school athletic complex and amenities building. Officials also announced that Algonquin will supply Chromebooks to all students in fall 2026 and implement bell-to-bell cell phone restrictions.

highlights.title: Architects launch revised Neary School renovation study
highlights.why: The Elementary School Building Committee initiated work with Tappé Architects following the earlier failed building proposal. The team plans to develop a menu of tiered renovation options, and architects advised that the October Special Town Meeting will likely serve as an informational update rather than a full funding vote.

highlights.title: Support staff labor agreements and superintendent raise approved
highlights.why: The Southborough and Regional school committees ratified collective bargaining agreements with Unit C educational support professionals and high school custodians. Combined school committees also rated Superintendent Greg Martineau exemplary and voted to grant him a 3.5 percent salary increase for the 2026-2027 school year.

highlights.title: FY27 municipal pay rates approved amid evaluation concerns
highlights.why: The Personnel Board approved municipal wage rates for FY27 while criticizing department heads for late performance evaluations that risk delaying raises. A proposal to grant an extra 2 percent raise outside the step system to an employee who reached the top step failed on a 2-2 tie vote.

highlights.title: Health survey shows substance drop but female and LGBTQ+ mental health gaps
highlights.why: The 2025 MetroWest Adolescent Health Survey revealed significant decreases in student substance use alongside concerns about smartphone overuse. The data showed persistent disparities in stress and anxiety among female, LGBTQ+, and minority students, which districts can address through grant funding.
highlights.body: Northborough, Southborough, and Regional School Committees and Superintendency Union #3
